capability_investigated:
WhisperProcessor feature extraction and the batch shape that generate()
accepts: input_features is a fixed 30s (3000-frame) log-mel per call, and
generate(features, prompts) takes a stacked (N, mel, 3000) feature batch
with one prompt list per window.
what_i_learned:
The stub's single processor(audio) call hard-truncates each recording to
30 seconds — anything past the first window is never fed to the model, so
the dominant error is deletion of the entire tail, not a decode-quality
problem. Batching N stacked 30s windows through one generate() call returns
N independent result objects, one per window.
hypothesis:
Slicing the waveform into consecutive non-overlapping 30s windows and
batch-decoding all of them recovers the deleted tail; concatenating the
per-window decodes should sharply raise length_ratio and cut deletion-driven
CER versus the single-window stub.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s batch dimension vs. GPU memory: how many stacked (mel, 3000)
windows one generate() call can hold before CUDA OOMs.
what_i_learned:
Batching ALL 30s windows of a full 0715 call-center recording into one
generate() call exceeds float16 CUDA memory and crashes (RuntimeError: CUDA
out of memory) — the recordings are long enough (many minutes) that the
window count blows the batch. Memory scales with batch size, so decoding one
window per generate() call bounds peak memory to a single window and still
recovers the full tail.
hypothesis:
Replace the single stacked batched generate() with a sequential loop that
decodes each consecutive 30s window in its own generate() call and joins the
per-window text, eliminating the OOM while preserving long-form coverage.

capability_investigated:
The input side of the pipeline rather than a decode knob — the raw waveform
passed to transcribe() before it reaches processor(). I derived per-frame RMS
energy (20ms frames) on the numpy audio to locate speech vs. silence, an
input the pipeline had never conditioned on. The audio profiles confirm the
signal is there: silence_ratio 6–25% and single silences up to 34s per file.
what_i_learned:
Fixed 30s windowing has two deletion sources independent of decode quality:
seams land mid-utterance (token loss at every boundary), and any window
carrying a long silence feeds that silence to the decoder, which is what
drives Whisper's repetition/hallucination collapse (repeated_text 0.36 on
best). Frame-energy VAD is computable with numpy alone (no silero/backend
dependency) and lets seams fall in silence while clear silence is dropped
from what the model ever sees.
hypothesis:
Replace blind fixed windows with energy-VAD windows: compute frame RMS,
threshold at peak−40dB, merge speech across <0.5s gaps, pad 0.25s, and pack
regions into <=30s windows that break only at silence (force-splitting any
single region longer than 30s). Cutting at silence removes boundary deletions
and feeding less silence should cut the repetition collapse that deletes
whole-window content — directly attacking the coverage/deletion axis while
keeping one-window peak memory.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return tokens when timestamps are ENABLED (prompt omits
<|notimestamps|>): the sequences_ids then interleave Whisper timestamp
tokens whose id maps linearly to a time offset, (id - timestamp_begin)*0.02s.
This is the return channel every prior iteration suppressed via
<|notimestamps|> + skip_special_tokens.
what_i_learned:
With timestamps on, each 30s window's decoded token stream reports where the
model thinks speech ended (the last timestamp token), giving a model-derived
boundary independent of any waveform-energy heuristic. timestamp_begin is
recoverable from the tokenizer as convert_tokens_to_ids("<|0.00|>"), so the
whole long-form seek loop is buildable through the frozen surface alone — no
silero/VAD and no direct ctranslate2 access needed.
hypothesis:
Replace energy-VAD segmentation with timestamp-guided sequential long-form:
decode a 30s window with timestamps, advance seek to the last emitted
timestamp, emit text only up to that segment, repeat. Boundaries chosen by
the model rather than by an energy threshold should stop dropping the span
after early/mis-placed seams, directly lifting length_ratio and cutting the
68% deletion mass.

capability_investigated:
The prompts argument of generate(): whether the per-window prompt list can
carry a <|startofprev|> context prefix (prior transcript tokens) ahead of the
<|startoftranscript|>/<|ko|>/<|transcribe|> SOT sequence, and whether
generate() returns only the freshly generated tokens (leaving timestamp
parsing intact) when given such a prefix.
what_i_learned:
Every prior iteration passed generate() only the bare SOT sequence as prompt,
leaving the decoder with zero running context — so cross-window term
consistency was never exploited. Whisper's prompt channel accepts a
<|startofprev|> token (recoverable via convert_tokens_to_ids) followed by
arbitrary prior-text token ids before SOT; this is the native
condition_on_previous_text mechanism and is reachable entirely through the
frozen surface (no direct ctranslate2 access).
hypothesis:
Carry the previous window's clean emitted text (capped at 224 tokens) as a
<|startofprev|> prompt prefix for the next window's decode. Conditioning on
running context biases consistent spelling of domain terms/names across
windows, attacking the dominant substitution axis (56%) without disturbing
the timestamp-seek coverage logic that already holds length_ratio at 0.94.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s return_scores and return_no_speech_prob kwargs and the
corresponding result fields (res.scores[0] = hypothesis log-probability,
res.no_speech_prob). Every prior iteration called generate() with only
beam_size/sampling_temperature and read only sequences_ids — the per-window
confidence channel was never requested or inspected.
what_i_learned:
ctranslate2's WhisperGenerationResult can return scores (a log-prob
confidence per hypothesis) and no_speech_prob alongside sequences_ids when
return_scores/return_no_speech_prob are passed. This makes a per-window
quality signal available through the frozen surface alone, which is the
prerequisite for any confidence-gated retry — the greedy pass otherwise has
no way to detect it committed to a wrong path.
hypothesis:
Replace the single greedy decode per window with a confidence-gated
temperature-fallback loop (temps 0.0/0.4/0.8): decode greedily, and if
avg log-prob < -1.0 or gzip compression ratio > 2.4 the window is re-decoded
with sampling at a higher temperature, escalating until it clears the gate.
Targets the substitution-dominant axis by letting low-confidence windows
(the worst-cer and hallucination files) escape the greedy basin instead of
emitting a confidently-wrong transcript; cost is bounded since only failing
windows retry.

capability_investigated:
The semantics of the multiple timestamp tokens within a single window's
sequences_ids (not just the last one). The timestamp channel (discovered
iter_004) carries every inter-segment boundary, so token_ids[ts_positions[-2]]
gives the penultimate boundary, letting me choose how many trailing segments
to commit vs. defer to the next window's overlap.
what_i_learned:
Each 30s window's right-edge final segment is the one Whisper decodes with the
least right-context, and the timestamp channel exposes enough boundaries to
defer it: advancing seek to the penultimate timestamp (instead of the last)
re-feeds that segment as an interior, fully right-contexted segment of the next
window. The penultimate-boundary offset also bounds the re-read cost — when it
lands >=20s in, the deferred tail is short, so window count stays <=1.5x.
hypothesis:
Substitution (56%, dominant; coverage healthy at len 0.94) is partly driven by
context-starved trailing segments. Ending each window one segment early so
every segment gets at least one decode where it is not the window's right edge
should lower substitution without re-introducing deletions.

capability_investigated:
How a window decode behaves under re-decoding: pairing generate()'s
return_scores channel (res.scores[0] = hypothesis avg log-prob, found
iter_006) with sampling_temperature>0 + sampling_topk=0 to draw a DIFFERENT
token path for the same audio, rather than the one fixed greedy path every
prior iteration committed to.
what_i_learned:
The greedy single-pass decode (beam_size=1, sampling_temperature=0.0) that
every prior pipeline used has no escape hatch — a window where greedy locks
onto a wrong token path stays wrong, which matches the substitution-heavy
profile (sub 57%, length_ratio 0.94 healthy). The scores channel plus a zlib
compression ratio over the decoded text are enough to gate a decode
(avg_logprob < -1.0 = low confidence, cr > 2.4 = repetition collapse), and
sampling_topk=0 with temperature>0 actually perturbs the path (topk=1 stays
greedy regardless of temperature), making a per-window re-decode loop
reachable entirely through the frozen surface.
hypothesis:
Re-decode any window that fails the avg-logprob/compression-ratio gate at an
escalating temperature (0.0->1.0 ladder) and keep the first gate-passing
attempt (else the highest-logprob one). Clean windows pass at t=0 so cost is
bounded; low-confidence/repetition windows get a chance to escape the bad
greedy commit, lowering substitution and fixing the repeated_text guard file.
